title: Soft-bridge sentinel and region circuit throttle hotfix
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production incidents in eu-west-1 revealed a pathological interaction between the regional circuit breaker and the connection router when a small cohort of long-lived requests produced KV-cache pressure and repeated reconnect churn. Impacted customers saw elevated 5xx spikes and slow tail latency during short regional flaps. Summary: add a lightweight 'soft-bridge sentinel' that preserves a minimal connection/kv lease for recently-evacuated routes and introduce a bounded regional circuit throttle to prevent rapid reopen cycles. This PR implements: 1) soft-bridge sentinel process that keeps an amortized keepalive token for connections that were recently proxied across region boundaries; 2) a bounded circuit throttle that enforces exponential reopen backoff with an upper cap and a per-route smoothing window; 3) telemetry hooks for bridge alive-counts and throttle-reset events; 4) a small configuration toggle (runtime flag) so SRE can opt the behavior in and out per-region; 5) unit + integration tests simulating short region flaps. Checklist: - [x] add sentinel loop and reconcile logic - [x] implement bounded throttle state machine - [x] expose metrics and traces - [x] add e2e scenario in perf-canary harness - [x] update runbooks and recovery steps - [x] smoke test on staging Why this is conservative: the sentinel only preserves a token (no full KV sync) and expires after a short TTL to avoid stale state; the throttle uses observed reopen density to avoid global stalls. Related: ENG-2147 (regional stability), SRE-389 (incident postmortem). Rolling strategy: squash-merge and immediate canary to a small percentage of eu-west-1 traffic, monitor sentinel.active and throttle.events. Risk: incorrect TTL could mask real failures, mitigated by telemetry and ability to toggle at runtime.
